<user_input mode="act">Implement Step 04 of PLAN.md (the web UI) for HintLab in this repo (/Users/prakharagarwal/ClineHackathon), plus the server-side fixes a tester found in the live Step 02 build. In the proof log this is Cline prompt 03 (web-ui). Build on the existing code (src/app.ts, src/agent.ts, src/sessions.ts, src/sse.ts, src/hintGuard.ts, src/allowlist.ts, src/runner.ts, scripts/check-runner.ts, scripts/check-agent.ts). Do not modify anything under cline-proof/.

A. Server-side SSE filtering (most important). The agent_text and reasoning events are unguarded model output and have leaked fixes (for example the corrected division for the average) to the browser. Fix this on the server, not just in the UI: GET /api/session/:id/stream must never send agent_text or reasoning events (and must not put model free text into any other event either, including tool_call/tool_result payloads of give_hint attempts that the guard rejected). Use an explicit allow-list of event types that may go to the client: test_results, tool_call (only for run_commands/read_files, with command or file name), tool_result (for run_commands: a short trimmed output summary; never the model's own text), approval (allowed/denied + command), hint (accepted, guarded hints only), hint_status/hint_rejected (no rejected text, just the reason category), status, error (friendly message only, see B), done. Keep the full raw events server-side only (for logs/debugging) if you want, but never stream them. Apply the same filter to the replay of past events.

B. Friendly errors. Turn raw error events into short human lines before they are sent, for example "Command blocked by allow-list: <command>", "Hint blocked: contained code, asking the tutor to rephrase", "Hint blocked: wrong level, asking the tutor to retry", "Tutor timed out, try again". No stack traces or raw SDK messages in the browser.

C. Web UI in web/ (plain HTML + CSS + vanilla JS, no build step, served by Express as static files at /). Clean, demo-ready on a projector: large readable fonts (base 18px+), high contrast, generous spacing, a simple header "HintLab: a debugging tutor that never writes the fix". Layout:
  1. Assignment picker (from GET /api/assignments) showing the statement and language; choosing one preloads its buggy starter code into an editable monospace textarea.
  2. "Run & get hint" button -> POST /api/session { assignmentId, code }; show the test results table (test name, input, expected, got, PASS/FAIL with colour, plus timeout/signal/build error info if present) from testResults.
  3. Live feed from GET /api/session/:id/stream (EventSource): only tool calls (the commands the tutor ran and their short results), test results, approvals and denials, hints and friendly status/error lines. Each item one short line with a small icon or label. Auto-scroll.
  4. Hint cards labelled "Level 1: nudge", "Level 2: where to look", "Level 3: the concept", appearing as each hint arrives. Hint text must be inserted with textContent (never innerHTML).
  5. Loading states: a spinner/"Tutor is reading your code..." while waiting for the first hint (typically 10-13 s), and "Thinking about the next hint..." after "Next hint" (typically 5-9 s). Disable the Next hint button while busy; if the server returns 409 show "Tutor is still busy, please wait" and keep the button disabled until the next hint/status arrives. After level 3 show "All hints given" and keep the button disabled. Starting a new run closes the old EventSource and resets the cards.
  6. Handle server errors (400/404/network) with a visible friendly message.

D. Smaller guard fixes (examples below are described in words on purpose; turn them into your own test strings):
  - Hint guard (src/hintGuard.ts): also block hints that embed a one-line code expression inside prose, with or without backticks. Examples the tester saw or expects: comparing a cleaned string variable for equality against its reversed slice; a range call that starts at one and ends at the length of the nums list; the sum variable divided by n; indexing nums with i; reversing s with a slice; and a C-style float cast of sum divided by n. In general: identifiers combined with code syntax such as call parentheses, square-bracket indexing or slicing, comparison or arithmetic operators between identifiers, casts, or semicolons. Stop the false positive on plain English prose such as the phrase "for x in the list" or "if the list is empty": programming keywords on their own are not code; only flag them when real code syntax is present. Add unit tests in scripts/check-agent.ts for both the new blocked cases and the prose that must pass.
  - Allow-list (src/allowlist.ts): deny any dollar sign anywhere in a command (variable or command expansion, for example echoing the HOME variable into the Python program), and remove the echo/printf pipe forms entirely so that no command containing a pipe character is allowed. Instead, when creating the agent workdir, write each test's input to its own file (named input-<test-name>.txt with a safe slug) and tell the agent in its prompt to feed those files to the program with a stdin redirect from that file name. Keep the other allowed forms: running python3 on main.py, the exact gcc build command from tests.json, running ./main, the stdin redirect from an input-*.txt file in the workdir, and cat of main.py, main.c, tests.json or an input-*.txt file. Update the allow-list unit tests so that echoing the HOME variable piped into the program, echoing a literal number piped into the program, a stdin redirect from a dollar-sign variable, and any other pipe are all denied.

F. Close the agent-side env leak found in 02c: the SDK's built-in run_commands runs student code on the host with the server's full environment and real HOME, so student code run by the agent could read server env vars or the ClinePass credentials in ~/.cline. Disable the built-in run_commands tool for the agent (enabled false in toolPolicies) and instead give the agent a custom run_tests tool (createTool + zod, via extraTools, auto-approved) that takes an optional test name and runs the student's code in its workdir through the hardened server runner (process-group kill, timeouts, minimal env with HOME set to the temp dir, signal reporting), returning per-test input, expected, got, stderr, signal and pass/fail. Keep the allow-list module and its unit tests, and keep requestToolApproval denying everything that is not explicitly allowed, so any command attempt is still blocked and shown as an approval-denied line. Show run_tests calls in the live feed as tool calls. Update check:agent to assert that run_commands was never executed and that run_tests was used or the tests were otherwise reported.

E. Checks. Keep npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner and npm run check:agent passing (update check:agent for the new SSE contract: it must assert that NO agent_text or reasoning events, and no rejected hint text, arrive over SSE, while hints at levels 1, 2 and 3 still arrive). Add scripts/check-web.ts with npm script "check:web" that starts the server on PORT=3200, fetches / and asserts the page loads (status 200, contains the app root/title, and that /app.js or whatever script it references and the CSS load with 200), fetches /api/assignments, starts one real session on is-palindrome or average-marks, reads the SSE stream until the level-1 hint (or a timeout), asserts the set of event types contains no agent_text/reasoning, prints the event types seen and the hint, and stops the server by PID. If a headless browser is already available you may also load the page in it, but do not install large browser downloads.

Update README.md (UI usage, SSE event contract, check:web).

Port rule: another tester may be using PORT=3100. Use PORT=3200 for all your server checks. Never kill, signal, or bind to processes on port 3100, no broad pkill patterns; stop only processes you started (by PID). Leave no server running at the end.

Verify before finishing: npm run typecheck, npm run test:runner, npm run check:agent, npm run check:web. Fix anything that fails and re-run. Report files changed, the SSE event types that now reach the client, the new allow-list, and the check outputs.</user_input>

1 | # HintLab
  2 | 
  3 | A debugging tutor for programming labs. A student pastes code and picks an
  4 | assignment; the server runs the code against the assignment's test cases in a
  5 | sandbox, then a Cline‑SDK agent diagnoses the failure and delivers **tiered
  6 | hints** (level 1 nudge → level 2 where to look → level 3 concept). It **never**
  7 | writes or reveals the fix.
  8 | 
  9 | This is **Step 02**: the HintLab tutor agent (built with `@cline/sdk`), wired
 10 | into the Express server. There is no web UI yet.
 11 | 
 12 | ## Requirements
 13 | 
 14 | - Node.js 22+ (verified on Node 24)
 15 | - Python 3 (`python3`) on PATH
 16 | - `gcc` on PATH (for the C assignment)
 17 | - A Cline CLI installation already authenticated with ClinePass (see
 18 |   [Agent credentials](#agent-credentials))
 19 | 
 20 | ## Install
 21 | 
 22 | ```sh
 23 | npm install
 24 | ```
 25 | 
 26 | ## Agent credentials (picked up from `~/.cline`)
 27 | 
 28 | The agent uses the same ClinePass provider/model as the Cline CLI:
 29 | 
 30 | - provider id: `cline-pass`
 31 | - model id: `cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro`
 32 | 
 33 | The SDK does **not** need an API key in the repo or in env vars. In local
 34 | backend mode (`backendMode: "local"`), `ClineCore.start` resolves credentials
 35 | itself from the Cline CLI's config/data directory:
 36 | 
 37 | - `~/.cline/data/settings/providers.json` → the `cline-pass` entry, whose
 38 |   `settings.auth` holds the OAuth `accessToken`/`refreshToken`. When
 39 |   `config.apiKey` is omitted, the SDK's local runtime host resolves the
 40 |   provider's OAuth token from this file (refreshing it if expired) and injects
 41 |   it for the request.
 42 | 
 43 | Treat `~/.cline` as read-only: the server never writes to it, and never logs
 44 | any token/secret (it only ever prints provider/model names). You can override
 45 | the provider/model via env vars:
 46 | 
 47 | ```sh
 48 | HINTLAB_PROVIDER_ID=cline-pass HINTLAB_MODEL_ID=cline-pass/deepseek-v4-pro npm start
 49 | ```
 50 | 
 51 | ## Start the server
 52 | 
 53 | ```sh
 54 | npm run dev      # watch mode
 55 | npm start        # run once (tsx src/server.ts)
 56 | ```
 57 | 
 58 | The server listens on `http://localhost:3000` by default. Override with `PORT`:
 59 | 
 60 | ```sh
 61 | PORT=3200 npm start
 62 | ```
 63 | 
 64 | ### Endpoints
 65 | 
 66 | | Method | Path                          | Description                                                      |
 67 | | ------ | ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
 68 | | GET    | `/api/health`                 | Liveness check                                                   |
 69 | | GET    | `/api/assignments`            | List assignments (id, language, statement, starter code)         |
 70 | | POST   | `/api/session`                | Run a submission + start the agent. Body `{ assignmentId, code? }` |
 71 | | GET    | `/api/session/:id/stream`     | Server-Sent Events (replay + live) for the session               |
 72 | | POST   | `/api/session/:id/next-hint`  | Ask the agent for the next hint level (2, then 3)                |
 73 | 
 74 | `POST /api/session` runs the sandboxed runner, creates a session, starts the
 75 | agent in the background asking for a **level‑1** hint, and immediately returns
 76 | `{ sessionId, testResults }`. If `code` is omitted, the assignment's starter
 77 | program is used. Unknown session ids return `404`; `next-hint` returns `409`
 78 | while the agent is still busy, and `{ level: 3, status: "complete" }` once all
 79 | three levels have been delivered.
 80 | 
 81 | ```sh
 82 | curl -s -X POST localhost:3200/api/session \
 83 |   -H 'content-type: application/json' \
 84 |   -d '{"assignmentId":"sum-of-list"}'
 85 | ```
 86 | 
 87 | ### SSE event types
 88 | 
 89 | The stream maps the SDK's `cline.subscribe` events (filtered by `sessionId`) to
 90 | these named events:
 91 | 
 92 | | Event            | Meaning                                                       |
 93 | | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
 94 | | `test_results`   | The runner's test results (inputs / expected / got)           |
 95 | | `agent_text`     | Assistant text (`content_start`/`content_end`, type `text`)   |
 96 | | `reasoning`      | Model reasoning summaries (if the provider emits them)        |
 97 | | `tool_call`      | A tool call started (name + input)                            |
 98 | | `tool_result`    | A tool call finished (name + output/error)                    |
 99 | | `approval`       | A `run_commands` approval decision (allowed/denied + commands + reason) |
100 | | `hint`           | An accepted hint delivered through `give_hint`                |
101 | | `hint_rejected`  | A hint rejected by the guard (wrong level or code detected)   |
102 | | `status`         | Session status / iteration / usage / notice updates           |
103 | | `error`          | An agent error (often recoverable)                            |
104 | | `done`           | The agent finished a turn                                     |
105 | 
106 | A `: ping` heartbeat comment is sent every ~15s; buffered events are replayed
107 | to late-joining clients.
108 | 
109 | ## Safety model
110 | 
111 | - The agent runs with `enableSpawnAgent: false` and `enableAgentTeams: false`.
112 | - All file-editing/network tools are disabled (`editor`, `apply_patch`,
113 |   `fetch_web_content`, `skills`, `ask_question`, `submit_and_exit` →
114 |   `{ enabled: false }`). `read_files` and `search_codebase` are auto-approved.
115 | - `run_commands` is `autoApprove: false` and gated by a strict regex allow-list
116 |   in `capabilities.requestToolApproval` (see `src/allowlist.ts`). Only the
117 |   assignment's own build/run/read commands are allowed; `;`, `&&`, `||`,
118 |   backticks, `$(`, extra pipes and other redirects are rejected. Every approval
119 |   decision is logged as an `approval` event.
120 | - Hints can only be delivered through `give_hint`, and every hint is checked by
121 |   `src/hintGuard.ts` before it is stored/sent. A hint containing a fenced code
122 |   block, long inline code, code-like lines, or a rewritten solution is rejected
123 |   (the model gets an error and rephrases without code).
124 | 
125 | ## Run the checks
126 | 
127 | ```sh
128 | npm run typecheck     # tsc --noEmit
129 | npm run test:runner   # sandboxed runner against the 3 buggy programs
130 | npm run check:agent   # end-to-end, REAL model call (starts a server on :3200)
131 | ```
132 | 
133 | `test:runner` runs the sandboxed runner against all three buggy starter programs
134 | and asserts the exact expected pass/fail of every test, plus a correct solution
135 | for each assignment, an infinite-loop program (must time out), and a C program
136 | with a compile error (must report a build failure).
137 | 
138 | `check:agent` unit-tests the allow-list (including injection attempts like
139 | `python3 main.py; rm -rf ~` and `cat /etc/passwd`) and the hint guard, then
140 | starts the server on `PORT=3200`, posts a `sum-of-list` session, reads the SSE
141 | stream, and requests hints level 2 and 3. It asserts exactly one accepted hint
142 | per level, that no hint contains code, that no edit/write tool was executed, and
143 | that any denied command was not run. It prints the hints verbatim, the distinct
144 | SSE event types, and the approval decisions, and exits non-zero on failure
145 | (overall timeout 8 minutes). It leaves no server running.
146 | 
147 | ## Typecheck / build
148 | 
149 | ```sh
150 | npm run typecheck   # tsc --noEmit
151 | npm run build       # tsc
152 | ```

export function checkHint(text: string): HintCheck {
  const t = text.trim();
  if (!t) return { ok: false, reason: "empty hint" };

  // 1. Fenced code blocks.
  if (t.includes("```")) return { ok: false, reason: "contains a fenced code block" };

  // 2. Inline code spans: allow only a short plain identifier (no syntax).
  for (const m of t.matchAll(/`([^`\n]+)`/g)) {
    const code = m[1].trim();
    if (!/^[A-Za-z_]\w{0,19}$/.test(code)) {
      return { ok: false, reason: "inline code is not a short plain identifier" };
    }
  }

  // 3. Whole-line source code (multi-line solution or a full statement).
  for (const line of t.split("\n")) {
    if (looksLikeCodeLine(line)) return { ok: false, reason: "text looks like source code" };
  }

  // 4. Code expressions embedded in prose (with or without backticks).
  if (hasEmbeddedCode(t)) return { ok: false, reason: "text contains a code expression" };

  return { ok: true };
}
